title: Shop on Amazon without the assistant
summary: There is no setting. On a computer an add-on removes it; on the phone it can only be ignored.
changes: On desktop, the assistant panel and its prompts are hidden. On mobile, nothing changes and we will not pretend otherwise.
how: Amazon's shopping assistant — originally Rufus, now folded into the search bar as Alexa for Shopping — has no account setting at all. Community add-ons hide the panel using ordinary page-blocking rules.
steps: Search your browser's add-on store for "Adios Alexa for Shopping" or "Rufus Remover".
On the phone, the only remedy is to use the mobile website in a browser with content blocking, or to ignore the prompt.
caveats: Amazon has moved and renamed this feature twice in two years; add-ons lag behind each change.
There is genuinely no way to turn it off in the Amazon mobile app.
Amazon's review summaries at the top of a listing are a separate generated feature, also not removable.

title: Skip the review summary, read the reviews
summary: Sort by most recent and filter to verified purchases to get past the generated digest.
changes: You read what people actually wrote, newest first, from confirmed buyers.
steps: On a product page, scroll to reviews and tap "See more reviews".
Change the sort from "Top reviews" to "Most recent".
Read the three-star reviews first; they are almost always the most informative.
how: The generated summary is built from the same reviews but flattens the disagreements, which are the part worth reading. Sorting by recency also catches products whose quality changed after a good early run.
caveats: Fake reviews exist regardless. Reviews mentioning specific, checkable details are the trustworthy ones.
Third-party checkers of review authenticity vary in quality; treat their scores as one signal.

title: Show handmade things only
summary: Etsy can restrict results to items the seller has declared handmade.
changes: Resold factory goods and print-on-demand listings drop out of the results.

action.label: Search handmade only
action.placeholder: A gift, a piece of jewellery, a print

how: Etsy records whether a seller declared an item handmade. The filter is not always shown in the interface, but the site honours it when asked for directly.
caveats: It relies on the seller's declaration, which is not audited. Generated artwork printed onto a mug can still be listed as handmade.
Check the shop's process photographs and reviews. Real makers show their workshop.
Etsy has removed and reinstated this filter from its visible interface before.

title: Marketplaces that ban generated work
summary: Smaller shops whose rules require the maker and the item to be real.
changes: Everything is made by a person, and the person is usually reachable.
how: These platforms vet sellers individually rather than by self-declaration, and several explicitly prohibit AI-generated designs in their terms.
caveats: Smaller catalogues and sometimes slower shipping.
Big Cartel hosts independent shops rather than acting as a marketplace, so there is no unified search.

title: Find the maker's own website
summary: The simplest way past a marketplace's machinery is to buy directly from the person.
changes: No recommendation engine, no summary, no fees taken from the maker, and usually a real email address.
how: Search for the name with the large marketplaces excluded. Most small makers have their own shop with better prices and more information about how things are made.
caveats: Small shops have less generous returns policies. Check before buying.
Use a payment method with buyer protection when buying from an unfamiliar site.

title: Compare prices without a chatbot
summary: Tools that show price history and stock, and nothing else.
changes: You see a graph of what a thing has actually cost over time, which settles most "is this a deal" questions.
how: Price history sites track listings over months and years. A sale price that matches the median is not a sale.
caveats: Coverage is best for Amazon and patchier elsewhere.

title: Buy second-hand from a person
summary: Used listings are written by individuals, photographed by them, and nothing about them is generated.
changes: Blurred kitchen-table photographs and honest descriptions of wear. Cheaper, and far more informative.
how: The link filters eBay to used condition, where private sellers dominate and listings are made by hand.
caveats: Private sales have fewer protections than retail. Use the platform's payment system, never a direct bank transfer.
Some professional resellers now use generated descriptions; the photographs give them away.
